tasks.short: Plan and guide experiential class projects

steps.what: Write the class projects plan with activities, timing and materials
Supervise students doing the experiential class projects
Guide students in learning from the activities through discussion and reflection

tasks.design: Reuse the existing class-project format in {DOCS} for activity sequence, timing and material headings. The teacher writes the project-specific content and retains practical supervision and learning discussion in full.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same plan structure is recreated for repeated class projects.
tasks.enabler_now: A native document template removes repeated layout without choosing the learning experience.
tasks.still_hard: A project must fit the learners and change when practical difficulties arise.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion during the activity and turn experience into learning.

ambition.what: The teacher keeps project design and live guidance.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reusable project-plan structures can reduce formatting while supervision and learning discussion remain live teaching.

assumptions: This is the statement's class-project alternative, including its actual working plan. OTHER means physical teaching space and project tools. Field-trip reservations and guest-speaker contracts are not assumed for an in-class project.
The teacher produces goals, timing and materials in s1 from existing course knowledge. The template supplies headings only, not invented student needs or an automatically safe activity.

s1 removes six units of repeated sequence and materials layout and retains24 for project content. Ordinary save within this document work is negligible and ungated. No new progress report is added after live guidance.
unknowns: Reuse of the current project format
research_questions: Which parts of an actual project plan repeat without changing the learning activity?

already_counted.description: Write the actual plan, supervise the activity and guide reflection

incremental.description: Keep the project template appropriate to current materials

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94 gross6 less upkeep1 gives5. For a novel project with little reusable sequence, plan writing retains29 of30, supervision40 and reflection30. Gross1 is offset by upkeep1, giving low0. No supervision or conversation saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in staff meetings and committees

steps.what: Read the required staff meetings agenda and committee papers
Attend staff meetings and contribute relevant teaching experience
Serve on committees through required discussion and collective decisions

tasks.design: Link the existing agenda and committee papers from the meeting entry in {CALENDAR} to their authoritative files in {DOCS}. The teacher reads the papers and participates in the required meetings and committee decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing can require finding papers across separate messages or folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native agenda links can remove file navigation without replacing reading or attendance.
tasks.still_hard: Required participation and collective decisions depend on colleagues' discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Bring classroom experience and exercise judgement with colleagues.

ambition.what: Required staff and committee participation remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: agenda links can shorten access to existing papers while required meeting participation remains unchanged.

assumptions: OTHER is the existing meeting room or call tool. Boundary is an ordinary committee member's preparation and participation, not chairing, minute taking or a new attendance report.
The existing meeting organiser already issues the agenda and papers. Linking them does not require new teacher data capture; the small added link maintenance is counted separately.
s1 removes1.5 units of file navigation and retains13.5 for reading. Meetings55 and committee contribution30 stay fully retained; no speculative shorter meeting is credited.
research_questions: Does the current invitation already open the authoritative papers directly?

already_counted.description: Read papers and participate in staff and committee work

incremental.description: Repair broken agenda links within the teacher's access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R98.5 gross1.5 less upkeep0.5 gives1. Where most papers are already linked, preparation retains14.5 of15 and all85 participation units remain; gross0.5 is consumed by upkeep0.5. No unkept record is added to create an opportunity.

tasks.short: Select, order and issue course supplies

steps.what: Select books, materials and supplies suitable for the course
Check existing books and supplies against course quantities
inputs: existing stock list and physical stock

steps.what: Prepare the complete materials order with quantities, prices and delivery destination
Check and authorise the final materials order within the actual purchasing mandate
Send only the authorised books and materials order to the selected supplier
Check delivered materials and issue the actual books and supplies to learners

tasks.design: Use an existing stock view in {OTHER} and reusable catalogue and destination fields in {PROCUREMENT}. The teacher checks real stock and quantities, an authorised purchasing officer checks the complete order, and the teacher sends that exact version before checking and issuing delivered materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing stock and recurring order fields are repeatedly found and re-entered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native stock views and catalogue order forms remove navigation and repeated entry without choosing teaching materials.
tasks.still_hard: Suitability, actual stock condition and correct physical distribution require attention.
tasks.human_edge: Choose materials that work for the learners and check what actually arrives.

ambition.what: Material choice and physical issue stay with the teacher.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: stock views and native catalogue forms can reduce repeated supply-order entry while selection, authorisation and issue remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means existing material stock tools and physical course supplies. Boundary includes selection, actual supplier order and later issue, with delivery occurring between s5 and s6.
The teacher verifies stock in s2; no live inventory sensor is assumed. Suppliers maintain catalogue descriptions and prices; the teacher verifies quantities and destination in s3.

s2 removes three units of stock-list navigation, retaining12 for actual checks. s3 removes nine units of repeated item and destination entry, retaining11 for quantities, substitutions and checks. Existing native functionality earns no new runtime saving.

The setting has an actual purchasing officer who authorises teacher requests. This is not author self-approval or a new approval of an internal save. s4 reviews the final items, quantities, prices, supplier and destination; any edit invalidates authority for s5. The current one-unit send remains fully retained.
unknowns: Whether stock and catalogue views already avoid duplicate entry
research_questions: Can an edited quantity or price invalidate the order's existing authorisation?

already_counted.description: Choose and verify materials, complete and send the actual order, check and issue delivery
Existing purchasing authority checks the complete order

approvals.approved_version: Exact final supplier, items, quantities, prices and delivery destination authorised in s4; edits require reauthorisation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B90 R78 gross13.333 less upkeep2 gives11.333; high11.3. For noncatalogue craft supplies with weak stock descriptions, stock work retains14 of15 and order entry18 of20. Three focal units saved over90 gives3.333 less upkeep2=1.333; low1.3. Officer time and the already small send receive no saving.

tasks.short: Assign and grade class work and homework

steps.what: Choose class work objectives, existing items and the marking key
Assemble chosen class work items and instructions into the assignment draft
Check the assembled homework, instructions, key and intended learner group
Publish only the checked homework to the intended class
Compare submitted closed class work answers with the verified key
Read open homework responses and assess reasoning and creative work
Check proposed marks and final feedback against the actual class work
Release the final grade and feedback for each student's class work

tasks.design: Use native exercise assembly and key-based closed-item marking in {LMS}; both produce drafts for the teacher. The teacher checks the complete assignment before issue, judges open responses and checks final marks and feedback before learner release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing exercises are copied into assignments and closed answers are compared manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assignment banks and fixed marking keys handle exact assembly and answer comparison without model judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Creative or ambiguous answers and educationally useful feedback require the teacher's assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise partial understanding and give feedback that helps this learner improve.

ambition.what: Use the available capacity for additional short checks of understanding, with their marking time counted as new demand.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed-answer work can be checked against a teacher-verified key, while open responses and final learner feedback require teacher judgement.

assumptions: The course actually uses both closed and open work and manually assembles existing items today. A purely creative course has less eligible work. This is informal course feedback, with no claim of autonomous certification.

The teacher supplies objectives, selected item ids and key in s1. Learners produce submissions only after issue; the LMS stores their actual answers. Learner completion is outside the teacher-labour boundary, not a cost transferred by the proposal.
s2 removes actual copying of selected bank items. s5 replaces actual fixed-key comparison, not subjective grading. Missing item links and unreadable responses stop for funded manual repair.

s3 and s7 are the teacher's substantive checks of assembled work and proposed marks before actual releases, not approvals of ordinary author saves. Each action binds the exact checked content and learner group; edits invalidate the release snapshot. Both one-unit release actions remain fully retained. Internal saving is ungated and earns no saving.
Native marking or assembly already used earns no new benefit. Access and any deployment obligations need confirmation for this provider before rollout; no student text is sent to a model.
unknowns: Existing use of native item banks and marking
research_questions: Does the native key preserve partial-credit exceptions for teacher review?

already_counted.description: Choose objectives and key, check the assembled assignment, assess open responses, verify final feedback and release

incremental.description: Maintain item keys and mappings and manually repair failed assembly or answer capture

approvals.approved_version: Exact assembled assignment, instructions, key and learner group checked in s3; edits require another check
Exact learner, final marks and feedback checked against submitted work in s7; edits require another check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R65 gross35 less upkeep5 gives30. With poorly linked bank items and many acceptable answer variants, assembly retains8 of10 and closed marking19 of25. All65 other units remain; R92 gross8 less upkeep5 gives3. There is no saving on the ordinary save or the two already small learner releases.
